Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:1.english: Lest he forget and go out - After nightfall.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:2.hebrew: ולא יפלה את כליו - מבער כנים מבגדיו, דמתרגמינן ״בערתי״ — ״פליתי״ (דברים כו). ולקמן (שבת יב.) מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:2.english: And one may not delouse his garments - [That is,] removing lice from his garments, as we translate [in the Targum]: "I have removed" [bi'arti, as] "I have cleared out" [paliti] (Deuteronomy 26). And below (Shabbat 12a), it explains the reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:3.hebrew: ולא יקרא לאור הנר - בספר, שמא יטה הנר להביא השמן לפי הפתילה שידלק יפה, ונמצא מבעיר בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:3.english: And one may not read by the light of the lamp - [This refers to reading] in a book, lest he tilt the lamp to bring the oil to the mouth of the wick so that it will burn well, and he will turn out to be kindling on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:4.hebrew: החזן - חזן הכנסת המקרא שבעה הקוראים בתורה. ופעמים שאינו יודע היכן צריכין לקרות למחר, ורואה היכן קורין תינוקות של בית רבן בשבת זו — והן קורין בסדר לאור הנר בבית הכנסת — ויודע שהיא פרשה של שבת זו. ל"א: חזן — מלמד תינוקות, ורואה היכן יתחילו למחר והיכא יסיימו פרשיותיהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:4.english: The attendant - The synagogue attendant who prompts the seven who read from the Torah. And at times he does not know where they need to read tomorrow, so he looks [to see] where the schoolchildren are reading on this Shabbat — and they read in order, by the light of the lamp in the synagogue — and [thereby] knows that it is the portion of this Shabbat. Another explanation: [The word] chazzan [means] a teacher of children, and he looks [to see] where they will begin tomorrow and where they will conclude their portions.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:5.english: Similarly - [It was] to make a distancing from transgression that they said [this].

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:6.english: The zav may not eat with the zava - And all the more so a [ritually] pure [man] with the zava.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:7.hebrew: מפני הרגל עבירה - מפני שמתוך שמתיחדין, יבא לבעול זבה, שהיא בכרת:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:10:7.english: Because of habituation to sin - Because, since they seclude themselves, he will come to have relations with a zavah, which is [punishable] by karet.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:11:1.hebrew: לא יעמוד אדם - ברה"י ויושיט פיו וראשו לרה"ר לאחוז כלי ולשתות — גזרה שמא יוציא הכלי אליו, ונמצא מתחייב חטאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:11:1.english: A person may not stand - [That is, stand] in the private domain and extend his mouth and head into the public domain to hold a vessel and drink — [this is] a decree lest he bring the vessel to himself, and he will turn out to be liable for a sin-offering.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:1:1.hebrew: עשרים ושש דכתיב שתים עשרה שנה עבדו את כדרלעומר - אין זו שלוה. וי"ג מרדו — אין זו שלום, שהיו בהן מלחמות. הרי כ"ה שנים, ושנת כ"ו נהרג כדרלעומר, והיתה בשלוה כ"ו הנותרים מנ"ב:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:1:1.english: Twenty-six, as it is written: “Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer” - This was not tranquility. And “thirteen [years] they rebelled” — this was not peace, for there were wars during them. Behold, [these are] twenty-five years, and [in] the twenty-sixth year Chedorlaomer was killed, and [Sodom] was in tranquility [for] the twenty-six [years] remaining from fifty-two.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:2:1.english: To uplift the house of our God - And through this, we merited [the continuation of the verse]: “to give us a wall in Judah.”

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:2:2.english: Kashkushei and abrurei - [These are] turrets and towers.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:2:3.hebrew: רב אשי - ראש ישיבה היה במתא מחסיא, ומנעם מלהגביה בתיהם יותר מבהכ"נ:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:2:3.english: Rav Ashi - He was the head of the yeshiva in Mata Meḥasya, and he prevented them from raising their houses higher than the synagogue.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:3:2.english: And not under a stranger - [These are] the Edomites [the Romans], who were more wicked.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:3:3.english: Ḥabar - A nation from among the Persians.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:3:4.hebrew: תלמיד חכם - אם יקניטנו, יענישנו. וכן יתום ואלמנה, מפני שדמעתן מצויה:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:3:4.english: Torah scholar - If [one] provokes him, he will punish him; and likewise [with] an orphan and a widow, because their tears are readily shed.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:4:1.hebrew: חולי - הוא חולי ארוך, המנוונה והולך ומתיש כח, כגון אשתא וחולי הראש:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:4:1.english: Illness - It is a prolonged illness that progressively wastes [one] away and saps [one's] strength, such as fever and an illness of the head.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:4:2.hebrew: כאב - הוא ההולך ובא, כגון כאב שן, כאב מכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:4:2.english: Pain - This is [pain] that comes and goes, such as a toothache [or] the pain of a wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:4:3.hebrew: מיחוש - חששא בעלמא, לפי שעה וקל:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:4:3.english: An ache - A mere ache, temporary and mild.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:5:1.hebrew: חללה של רשות - עומק לבם, שהוא צריך להיות לו לב לכמה מדינות, למס הקצוב, ולכמה מלחמות, ולכמה משפטים — והכל ביום אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:5:1.english: The expanse of the ruling authority - The depth of their heart, for he needs to have a heart [attentive] to many provinces, to the fixed tax, and to many wars, and to many judgments — and all in a single day.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:7:1.hebrew: עיגלא תילתא - שלישי לבטן, שהוא משובח, מפני שהבהמה בקטנותה אינה עדיין בכחה, והולד ראשון ושני אינו בריא:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:7:1.english: A third-born calf - The third [offspring] of the womb, which is of superior quality, because an animal in its youth is not yet at its full strength, and the first and second offspring are not healthy.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:8:1.hebrew: והא תנא ליה רישא אם התחילו אין מפסיקין - וגבי תפלה קיימינן, ולמה ליה למיהדר למיתני ואין מפסיקין לתפלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:8:1.english: But didn't he teach in the first clause, “If they began, they do not stop” - And we are dealing with prayer, so why did he need to go back and teach: “And they do not stop for prayer”?

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:8:2.english: We have arrived at words of Torah - And [the Tanna] took up a different matter.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:8:3.hebrew: חברים העוסקין בתורה מפסיקין - תורתן לקריאת שמע, דזמנה דאוריי' — ״ובשכבך ובקומך״ — ואין מפסיקין לתפלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:8:3.english: Scholars who are engaged in Torah [study] interrupt - [They interrupt] their Torah [study] for the recitation of the Shema, since its time is from the Torah — "when you lie down and when you rise up" — and they do not interrupt [it] for prayer.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:8:4.hebrew: אבל אנו - הואיל ומפסיקין תורתנו לאומנתנו, כ"ש שנפסיק לתפלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:8:4.english: However, we - Since we interrupt our Torah [study] for our occupation, all the more so should we interrupt for prayer.

Rashi on Shabbat 11a:9:1.hebrew: עיבור שנה - שהיו עולים שבעה לעלייה, ונושאין ונותנין אם השנה ראויה וצריכה להתעבר, כדאמר בסנהדרין (יא:): על האביב, ועל פירות האילן, ועל התקופה:
Rashi on Shabbat 11a:9:1.english: The intercalation of the year - For seven [judges] would ascend to the upper chamber and deliberate whether the year was fit and needed to be intercalated, as it says in Sanhedrin (11b): "On account of the spring [crop], on account of the fruit of the tree, and on account of the equinox."

Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:10:1.hebrew: שמא ישכח ויצא - אליבא דרבא, דאמר לא גזרי גזירה לגזירה — אין לפרש שמא ישכח המחט, דאפילו יצא, ליכא איסור דאורייתא; כדאיתא בפ"ב דב"ק (דף כו:): "הכיר בה ושכחה — לענין שבת פטור, מלאכת מחשבת אסרה תורה". אלא שמא ישכח את המחט להצניעו עד שיהיה שבת, ולבסוף כשיזכור את המחט — ישכח שהוא שבת ויצא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:10:1.english: "Lest he forget and go out" - According to Rava, who says that we do not issue a decree upon a decree, one cannot explain [this as meaning] lest he forget the needle [and go out with it], for even if he were to go out, there is no Torah prohibition [violated], as it is stated in the second chapter of Bava Kamma (26b): "[If] he was aware of it and forgot it — regarding Shabbat he is exempt, [for] the Torah prohibited intentional labor [melekhet maḥashevet]." Rather, [it must mean:] lest he forget to put the needle away until it is Shabbat, and ultimately, when he remembers the needle, he will forget that it is Shabbat and go out.

Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:11:1.hebrew: לא יעמוד אדם ברה"ר וישתה ברה"י - בהמוצא תפילין (נ. ירובין דף צט.) מוקי לה בחפצים הצריכים לו, ודברי הכל. פי' אפי' רבנן דאמרי עומד אדם בר"ה ומטלטל ברה"י — הכא מודו, דכיון דצריך לשתות איכא למיחש שמא יביאם אצלו. וא"ת: השתא נמי, כי יכניס ראשו ורובו אמאי שרי? הא מפיק מרה"י לרה"ר, שלוקח ברה"י ונחית בבטנו ברה"ר! דהכי אמר התם: השתין מים ורק — חייב חטאת. ויש לומר: דבליעתו היינו הנחתו, ואין לחוש במה ששוב נכנסים לתוך מעיו; כדאמר (לקמן שבת דף כ.): הוציא דיו לכתוב ב' אותיות וכתבן כשהוא מהלך — חייב, דכתיבתן זו היא הנחתן. ואתי שפיר הא דפרק אמרו לו (כריתות דף יג:): יש אוכל אכילה אחת וחייב עליה ד' חטאות ואשם אחד, רבי מאיר אומר: אף אם היתה שבת והוציאו בפיו — חייב. והשתא, היכי תני ר"מ הוצאה, דלא מחייב עלה עד שתנוח במעיו, בהדי הנהו דמחייב בשעת בליעה? אלא אהוצאה מחייב נמי בשעת בליעה, כדפרישית. ורש"י תירץ בענין אחר בהמוצא תפילין (עירובין דף צט:), ובפ"ב דעירובין (דף כ. ושם) פירשתי. ונראה, דאע"ג דהלכה כר"מ בגזרותיו, בהא דאמר לא יעמוד ברה"ר ומטלטל ברה"י או איפכא — לית הלכתא כוותיה, אלא כרבנן דשרו; כדמוכח בהמוצא תפילין (שם דף צח:), דאמר מתני ליה רבי חנינא בר שלמיא לחייא בר רב קמיה דרב לא יעמוד כו', א"ל: שבקת רבנן ועבדת כר"מ:
Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:11:1.english: "A person may not stand in the public domain and drink in the private domain" - In [the chapter] HaMotzei Tefillin (Eruvin 99a), [the Gemara] establishes this as [referring to] items that he needs, and [this is according to] everyone. Explanation: Even the Rabbis, who say [that] a person may stand in the public domain and move [objects] in the private domain, agree here; for since he needs to drink, there is reason for concern lest he bring them to himself. And if you say: Now too, when he introduces his head and most of his [body into the private domain], why is it permitted? Isn't he carrying out from the private domain into the public domain, since he takes [the liquid] in the private domain and it descends into his stomach in the public domain? For so [the Gemara] said there: One who urinated or spat is liable to bring a sin-offering! And one can say [in reply]: His swallowing is its placement, and there is no need for concern about the fact that it subsequently enters into his entrails; just as [the Gemara] says (below, Shabbat 80a): One who carried out ink [sufficient] to write two letters, and wrote them while walking, is liable, for their writing is their placement. And [according to this,] that which is taught in the chapter [entitled] Amru Lo (Keritot 13b) works out well: "There is [a case where one] eats a single eating and is liable for it four sin-offerings and one guilt-offering... Rabbi Meir says: Even if it was Shabbat and he carried it out in his mouth, he is liable." Now, how could Rabbi Meir teach [liability for] carrying out — for which one is not liable until it comes to rest in his entrails — together with those [prohibitions] for which one is liable at the moment of swallowing? Rather, for carrying out one is also liable at the moment of swallowing, as I explained. And Rashi answered in a different manner in HaMotzei Tefillin (Eruvin 99b); and in the second chapter of Eruvin (20b, and see there), I explained [this]. And it appears that even though the halakha follows Rabbi Meir in his decrees, in this [matter], where he said [that] a person may not stand in the public domain and move [objects] in the private domain, or vice versa, the halakha does not follow him, but rather the Rabbis, who permit [it]; as is proven in HaMotzei Tefillin (ibid. 98b), where [the Gemara] states: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Shelamya was teaching to Ḥiyya bar Rav before Rav: "A person may not stand...", [and Rav] said to him: "Have you abandoned the Rabbis and acted in accordance with Rabbi Meir?!"

Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:3:1.hebrew: ולא תחת חבר - פירש בקונטרס: חבר — פרסיים. ול"נ, דפרסיים היו בבבל מימות כורש, כדפירש"י בפ"ב דגיטין (דף יז.), וחברים בימי רבי יוחנן אתו לבבל, כדאמר בהבא על יבמתו (יבמות סג:). ועוד, דאמרינן בקדושין (עב.): "הראני פרסיים — דומין לחיילות בית דוד; הראני חברין — דומין למלאכי חבלה", משמע דחברי אומה אחרת היא. והא דאמר בפרק ב' דגיטין (דף ז.): "אתא חברא שקל שרגא מקמייהו, אמר רחמנא: או בטולך או בטולא דבר עשו; למימרא דבני אדומים מעלי מפרסיים? והתניא: 'אלהים הבין דרכה וגו'' — ידע הקב"ה שאין ישראל יכולים לקבל רוב גזרותיו של עשו הרשע, עמד והגל' אותם לבבל" — לאו משום דחברים היו פרסאי, אלא עיקר היו הפרסיים, והחברים שביניהם היו כפופין להן. ומשני: "הא מקמי דאתו חברי לבבל" — היו פרסאי מעלו מרומאי; והא דקאמר "או בטולך או בטולא דבר עשו" — בתר דאתו חברי לבבל בימי ר' יוחנן, כדמוכח בהבא על יבמתו (יבמות סג:), והרשיעו את הפרסיים, דרומיים מעלי מפרסאי. ורש"י פירש שם ד"אתו חברי לבבל" — פרסיים בימי כורש; ול"נ כדפרישי', דהא בימי רבי יוחנן אתו חברי, ופרסיים בימי כורש, וכדמוכח בקדושין (דף עב.) דלאו אומה אחת הן. והר"ר יעקב מקורביל מפרש, דחברים היו משרתים מפרסיים, דומים למלאכי חבלה לפי שלובשים בגדים שחורים ורחבים; והיינו דשקל הכומר שרגא להביא לע"ז שלהן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:3:1.english: "And not under a chabar" - The Kuntres explained: Chabar [means] Persians. And it does not appear [correct] to me, for the Persians were in Babylonia from the days of Cyrus, as Rashi explained in the second chapter of Gittin (17a), whereas the chabarim came to Babylonia in the days of Rabbi Yochanan, as [the Gemara] says in Haba Al Yevamto (Yevamot 63b). And furthermore, we say in Kiddushin (72a): "Show me Persians — [they] resemble the legions of the House of David. Show me chabarin — [they] resemble angels of destruction." This implies that the chabari are a different nation. And that which [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Gittin (17a [cited as 7a]): "A chabara came and took the lamp from before them. [Rabba] said: 'Merciful One, either in Your shadow or in the shadow of the son of Esau!' Is this to say that the descendants of Edom (the Romans) are better than the Persians? But isn't it taught: 'God understands its way...' (Job 28:23) — The Holy One, Blessed be He, knew that Israel cannot endure most of the decrees of the wicked Esau, so He arose and exiled them to Babylonia!" — [this was asked] not because chabarim were Persians, but rather the Persians were primary, and the chabarim who were among them were subordinate to them. And [the Gemara] resolves: "That was before the chabarim came to Babylonia" — [at that time,] the Persians were preferable to the Romans; whereas that which he said: "Either in Your shadow or in the shadow of the son of Esau" was after the chabarim came to Babylonia in the days of Rabbi Yochanan, as is proven in Haba Al Yevamto (Yevamot 63b), and they made the Persians wicked, so that the Romans were [now] preferable to the Persians. And Rashi explained there that "the chabarim came to Babylonia" [refers to the arrival of the] Persians in the days of Cyrus; but it does not appear [correct] to me, [and rather it is] as we have explained: for the chabarim came in the days of Rabbi Yochanan, while the Persians [came] in the days of Cyrus, and as is proven in Kiddushin (72a) that they are not one nation. And Rabbeinu Yaakov of Corbeil explains that the chabarim were ministers [priests] of the Persians, [who] resemble angels of destruction because they wear black and wide garments; and this is why the priest took the lamp to bring [it] to their idol worship.

Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:8:1.hebrew: כגון רבי שמעון בן יוחי וחבריו - והא דאמר לקמן (דף לג:): "כי הוה מטי (זמן תפלה) לביש ומכסי ומצלי" — ההוא מצלי היינו ק"ש:
Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:8:1.english: "Such as Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai and his colleagues" - And that which [the Gemara] says later (33b): "When (the time of prayer) arrived, he would dress, cover himself, and pray" — that "he would pray" means the recitation of the Shema.

Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:8:2.hebrew: כגון אנו מפסיקין בין לקריאת שמע בין לתפלה - והא דאמר ליה רבי זירא לרבי ירמיה: "מסיר אזנו משמוע תורה וגו'" — וי"ל: תורתו היתה אומנתו, או עדיין לא היתה שעה עוברת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:8:2.english: "The likes of us interrupt both for the recitation of Shema and for prayer" - And [as for] that which Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Yirmeya: “One who turns his ear from hearing Torah, etc.” [when Rabbi Yirmeya hurried to pray] — one can say: His Torah was his occupation; or, the time [for prayer] was not yet passing.

Tosafot on Shabbat 11a:9:1.english: Regarding the intercalation of the year - So that the festivals will not be disrupted.
